REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 13, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
Council Chamber, Bloomfield and 183rd Street
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT HELD ON APRIL 13,
2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Reverend Joseph H. Lao, First Evangelical
  Community Church Cerritos Campus.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by the Leal Elementary School Businesses
  Assisting Students in Educational Success (BASES) Program participants.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations presented to:

  Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Deputy Mark Smith (Twenty-eight years of service)

  Dr. Mary Sieu (Region 14 Superintendent of the Year and California State
  Superintendent of the Year)

  Haskell Middle School, Carmenita Middle School, and Tetzlaff Middle School
  (Schools to Watch – Taking Center Stage)

  Councilmember Carol Chen presented plaques to her appointees to City
  Commissions and Committees in appreciation for their fine service. The
  following individuals were recognized:

  Doris Iglesias – Fine Arts and Historical Commission
  Victor Gau – Community Safety Committee
  Waldo Arballo –Property Preservation Commission
  Richard Li – Let Freedom Ring Committee
  Rosalinda Law – Economic Development Commission
  Gordon Hom – Community Safety Committee
  James Yee – Parks and Recreation Commission
  Chuong Vo – Planning Commission/Community Safety Committee
  Jennifer Hong – Let Freedom Ring Committee
 City of Cerritos  April 13, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 8

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

  Mayor George Ray presented plaques to his appointees to City Commissions
  and Committees in appreciation for their fine service. The following individuals
  will be recognized:

  Janet Beach – Fine Arts and Historical Commission
  Larry Constantino – Community Safety Committee
  Timothy Coomes – Community Safety Committee
  Janice Dawson – Let Freedom Ring Committee
  Philip Hickok – Property Preservation Commission
  Becky Lingad – Planning Commission
  Dan Padelford – Economic Development Commission
  Jack Reidy – Parks and Recreation Commission
  Lewie Woodson – Let Freedom Ring Committee

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Katherine Chu spoke regarding State Autism Month.

  Bob Buell thanked the Council and staff for their successful conclusion of the
  settlement with the State, and congratulated the Water Department on a quick
  completion of reclaimed water line repairs.

  Chris Craig, representing Assemblymember Christina Garcia, announced an Earth
  Day event.

  Andrew Johnson expressed concerns with the profitability of the Cerritos Center for
  the Performing Arts, crime in the community, and the feasibility for the car museum.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of March
  20, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of March 20, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 13, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated April 13, 2017
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated April 13, 2017 in the amount of
  $12,574,879.40 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated April 13, 2017 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency
  dated April 13, 2017 in the amount of $13,515,287.26 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending February 28, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending February 28, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of a contract for playground improvements at Friendship and Brookhaven
  parks, Project No. 10073, Bid No. 1291-17 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to reject all bids and
  authorize staff to re-bid the project at a future date. The motion carried (5 - 0) as
  follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 13, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7F.  Award of a contract for Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts acoustic banner
  replacement, RFP No. 1296-17 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $61,029 for replacement of half of the
  acoustic banners and all of the red box curtains at the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts (base bid) to Black Sheep Enterprises; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract modifications
  that may be necessary to complete the specified scope of work (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7G.  Award of a contract for floor resurfacing at the Cerritos Center for the Performing
  Arts, Project No. 12719, Bid No. 1295-17 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $177,785 for floor resurfacing at the Cerritos
  Center for the Performing Arts (base bid), Project No. 12719, Bid No. 1295-17, to
  Petra CPS and reject the other bid; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7H.  Award of Bid No. 1289-17, mailing list acquisition services for the Cerritos
  Center for the Performing Arts (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to award Bid No. 1289-
  17 to Response Solutions of Danbury, Connecticut, for the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts Mailing List Acquisition Services. In the event issues of non-
  performance arise, the agreement would be rescinded from Response Solutions and
  given to the next lowest bidder to ensure the City’s deadlines, quality standards and
  specifications are met. This process would be repeated as necessary in order of the
  lowest bid to the highest (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 13, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7I.  Award of a contract for Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course netting canopy
  installation, RFP No. 1294-17 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $47,800 for Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf
  Course Netting Canopy Installation, RFP No. 1294-17, to Judge Netting; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of a request for authorization for the City of Cerritos
  (Seller) to enter into negotiations to sell city-owned property located at 17423
  Studebaker Road, Cerritos, California, 90703, to Lou Sobh Cerritos Saturn, Inc.
  (Buyer), for Cerritos Auto Square related purposes (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Yosemite Hamilton, Kia of Cerritos Controller, responded to inquiries from the City
  Council regarding this matter.

  Anantha Ramachandran expressed concerns regarding the timing of the sale of this
  property.

  Jay Gray expressed concerns regarding the timing of the sale of this property.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Chen, to authorize the City
  Manager, or his designee, to enter into negotiations to sell City-owned property
  located at 17423 Studebaker Road, Cerritos, California, 90703, to Lou Sobh
  Cerritos Saturn, LLC., and/or designee (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido
  NOES:  Solanki, Ray
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 13, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration of award of contract to CalMet Services, Inc.
  for the solid waste management services in the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Mike O’Grady, Environmental Services Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Jay Gray requested transparency into the City's bidding process.

  JB Blackman-D'Souza, Vice-President of CalMet Services, Inc., responded to inquiries
  from the City Council.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to execute an
  agreement with CalMet Services, Inc. for Integrated Solid Waste Management
  Services in the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an agreement between Union Pacific Railroad Company
  and the City of Cerritos for the purpose of re-aligning an existing sewer line
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize the City
  Manager to execute the agreement between the Union Pacific Railroad Company
  and the City of Cerritos and remit a payment of $24,000 to Union Pacific
  Railroad Company for the processing of the agreement. Upon execution of the
  agreement, staff will seek reimbursement from Caltrans for the agreement
  processing fee (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 13, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Consideration of a lease agreement between the City of Cerritos and B&B Stables
  for the use of the five-acre City-owned parcel located east of the San Gabriel river
  channel, west of Dumont Avenue between 183rd Street and Artesia Boulevard (APN
  7034-018-901) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherre Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Mary Buell, property owner, spoke in support of the project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1. Approve the lease agreement between the City of Cerritos and B&B stables
  for the use of a five-acre City-owned parcel located east of the San Gabriel
  River Channel, west of Dumont Avenue between 183rd Street and Artesia
  Boulevard (APN 7034-018-901) with an initial commencement date of May 1,
  2017 and a termination date of April 30, 2022; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the lease agreement (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Pulido, Chen, and Edwards, Mayor
  Pro Tem Solanki, and Mayor Ray.

12.  Closed Session

  None.
 City of Cerritos  April 13, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 8 of 8

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:48 p.m., in memory of Gary Paul Kauble and
  Hermy Alonzo.
